The decision to file the NDA for a Traditional Approval follows a pre-NDA meeting held this fall with the FDA.
The Company’s decision to submit the NDA followed an End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA in September 2025 and a follow-up Type C meeting in January 2026.

Important factors that could cause such differences include, among others, the risk that the FDA will refuse to file the NDA or will not approve ifetroban, including because of concerns about the LVEF endpoint, the natural-history comparator or the statistical analysis plan; the risk that the FDA will not agree with Cumberland's interpretation of the minutes or outcomes of its meetings with the FDA; the risk that the FDA will require a Phase 3 trial or other additional studies or data, which could significantly delay or prevent approval and require substantial additional capital; the risk that data from the open-label extension, including the 24- and 36-month MRI analyses, will not be favorable; Cumberland's ability to meet the FDA's other approval requirements, including chemistry, manufacturing and controls requirements; the risk that rolling review will not shorten the review timeline; restrictions that may be placed on the label, if approved; changes in FDA requirements, policies or regulatory pathways; and the risks described under the heading "Risk Factors" in Cumberland's most recent Form 10-K and subsequent Form 10-Q filings, as well as other reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
